notes:
- Vertical: fintech payments + approvals; latency critical for fraud chatflows
- Workload mix: ~60% short-chat (16-64 tokens), 30% embeddings for similarity, 10% reranking for rules/alerts
- Performance targets: 99th% latency <150ms for 64-token chat; median <40ms; throughput target 200–300 rps in steady state
- Cost sensitivity: emphasis on unit economics. Goal: reduce inference cost by >=3x vs current managed endpoint via batching + 4-bit quantization + KV caching
- Model preferences: prefer open models but not dogmatic — currently experimenting with LLaMA2-70B-4bit and Falcon-40B-8bit as fallback
- Routing/fallback: need automatic fallback to 13B variant for traffic spikes; policy must be transparent for SLAs
- Caching requirements: prefix/KV cache for repeated context across sessions (payments templates) + TTL controls; strong interest in cache hit metrics in Console
- Batching needs: sub-100ms batching window for low tail latency; want smart batching guidance from Redwood Optimize; will test different batcher configs in POC
- Quantization: require model quality baseline tests (ROUGE/semantic similarity) after 4-bit quant; not willing to accept >2% drop vs FP16 on critical prompts
- Observability: token-level cost attribution, per-model 99/95/50 latency histograms, trace IDs attached to user sessions
- Security: must support SSO/SAML, BYOK (KMS/HSM), audit logs for data access; on-prem deployment considered for EU/regulated customers
- Quote from CTO: "We can't trade away 99th% latency for cost. If Redwood's batching makes tail worse, we can't go live."
- Pricing sensitivity: procurement pushing for committed capacity discount; exploring Dedicated reserved + burst to hosted fallback
- POC metrics agreed: end-to-end 99th% latency, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, model output quality delta vs baseline
- Stubs: fireflies ff:20260215_572Q (sec call), gmail thread:1782945 (pricing), drive:/deals/pulseai/rdw_pricing_dedicated_2026.pdf (pricing deck)
